votes.conditions:
Verified in User Manual Issue 06 (2025-09-30):
(1) M1 firmware must be SUN2000MA V100R001C00SPC161 or later. This appears in the §2.3.1 note and in Table 2-4.
(2) M1 on/off-grid (backup) needs at least two Energy Storage Modules, so a 7-S1 with one 7-E1 is on-grid only. One correction: the claim's "backup kits need the LUNA2000-14-S1 or larger" is too narrow, because the 10-S1 (5+5) and 12-S1 (5+7) also have two modules. With the 7-E1 modules in the catalogue, the 14-S1 is the smallest two-module option.
(3) One module gives a maximum output of 3.5 kW (manual §9; the datasheet gives 3.5 kW for the 7-S1). The 10 kW inverter is therefore battery-limited to 3.5 kW.
(4) The TOU and Maximum self-consumption modes need a power meter, or a SmartAssistant or SmartGuard, at the grid connection point.
(6) "If more than two ESSs are connected to one inverter, the black start function is not supported."
Not supported as written: condition (5), "the RS485 baud rate must be 9600; reset it if first paired with an MB0". The manual only says to restore 9600 bps before powering off, or when replacing the ESS or inverter, if the ESS is connected to an MB0, LC0 or MAP0 inverter. It sets no 9600 requirement for the M1, so drop condition (5) or reword it.
Other notes: Huawei shows no Albania-specific restriction. The inverter specs page and the S1 specs page are the global ("en") editions; the /eu/ paths redirect to the home page. Neither the datasheet nor the specs page names a separate communication cable or gateway beyond the ESS's standard RS485 link to the inverter.

votes.reason:
I could not refute it. Huawei names this exact pair on both sides, with the right variants. (1) Inverter side: the official spec page for "SUN2000-3/4/5/6/8/10KTL-M1 (High Current Version)" says "Compatible battery model | LUNA2000-5/10/15-S0, LUNA2000-7/14/21-S1". That names S1, and 7-S1 specifically. (2) Battery side: the LUNA2000-5/7/10/12/14/15/17/19/21-S1 datasheet (Version 01-202509) lists among its compatible inverters "SUN2000-3/4/5/6/8/10KTL-M1". I extracted that text from the PDF myself. The live LUNA2000-7/14/21-S1 spec page says the same. Its timetable footnote 9 covers only the LC0 and L1 inverters, not the M1. The same datasheet confirms that the 7-S1 is one LUNA2000-10KW-C1 power module plus one LUNA2000-7-E1 (6.9 kWh). That matches the catalogue item exactly. (3) The LUNA2000-S1 User Manual is Issue 06, dated 2025-09-30, and I confirmed that on the PDF title page. It treats the SUN2000-(3KTL-10KTL)-M1 as a supported inverter, with conditions. (4) As a counter-check I read Huawei Digital Power Switzerland's guide "Anleitung Batterie und Backup" (10.11.2025). It says the LUNA2000-S1 "ist mit allen Hybridwechselrichtern von Huawei kompatibel" ("is compatible with all Huawei hybrid inverters") and gives the M1 COM pin-out for S1. I searched for a source saying S1 is incompatible with M1 or with older M1 hardware and found none. The only incompatibility in Huawei and distributor material is S0 and S1 battery modules mixed in one stack. That does not apply here. All sources date from 2023 or later.

None of the conditions makes the kit unusable as sold. Backup is not part of a panels + inverter + battery kit anyway, because the M1 needs the separate Backup Box-B1 for backup output. The firmware and meter requirements can be met in the field. The firmware string SPC161 appears only in the Huawei manual, and I found no independent release note for it. So the shop cannot assume units leave the warehouse on that firmware: the installer must check it at commissioning.

votes.conditions:
Model variants named: SUN2000-10KTL-M1 (spec page titled "High Current Version"; the manual covers the whole SUN2000-(3KTL-10KTL)-M1 range and the SUN2000-10KTL-BEM1). Battery is LUNA2000-7-S1 = LUNA2000-10KW-C1 + 1 × LUNA2000-7-E1 (S1, not S0; S0/E0 modules cannot be mixed with S1/E1).

Conditions, all confirmed in the S1 User Manual Issue 06 (2025-09-30):
(1) M1 firmware must be SUN2000MA V100R001C00SPC161 or later.
(2) "When the SUN2000-(3KTL-10KTL)-M1 is used in the on/off-grid scenario, at least two Energy Storage Modules are required". So the 1-module 7-S1 is on-grid only with this inverter. Never sell this kit as backup-capable. Backup also needs the separate BackupBox-B1 on the M1, per the inverter spec page.
(3) One module limits charge and discharge to 3.5 kW (datasheet).
(4) TOU and Maximum self-consumption modes need a power meter at the grid connection point, or a SmartAssistant/SmartGuard. Without one, the battery cannot do self-consumption, so the meter must be added to the kit. On the M1, the battery and the meter share the COM RS485-2 pins 7 and 9 (Swiss Huawei guide).
(5) The battery uses the three-phase operating window of 600–980 V, which matches the M1 battery input of 600–980 V. The M1 is three-phase only.
(6) Black start is not supported with more than two ESSs per inverter. This does not affect a single 7-S1.
(7) The 9600 bps baud-rate restore applies only when the ESS was previously on an MB0, LC0 or MAP0 inverter.
(8) The manual notes the 8KTL/10KTL-M1 is not for Australia. This does not affect Albania.

All sources are from 2023 or later (datasheet 01-202509, manual 2025-09-30, Swiss guide 2025-11-10). The inverter spec page is undated.

Unknown (never auto-pair): Fronius Symo GEN24 10.0 Plus + LUNA2000-7-S1, and Fronius Primo GEN24 5.0 Plus + LUNA2000-7-S1. Both researchers proposed not_compatible. Neither maker lists the pair, but neither states an exclusion either. Fronius's compatible-batteries page says its inverters support other makers' storage "such as BYD or LG", and its Primo manual has no "only approved batteries" sentence. Huawei's S1 datasheet just lists Huawei inverters. The voltage windows overlap. Under the matrix rule that is unknown.

CATALOGUE GAPS:
1. Growatt MOD 10KTL3-XH has no compatible battery in the catalogue. Growatt's current manual (MOD_3-10KTL3-XH_User_Manual_EN_202405, en.growatt.com) says "Compatible battery (only) ARK-XH HV Battery" with a 600-950 V port. The BP variant takes "APX HV Battery (only)". To sell Growatt kits, add the ARK-XH (plus its BDC) or the APX HV for the BP variant.
2. BYD HVS 10.2 is explicitly excluded on the Primo GEN24 5.0 Plus; only HVS 5.1 and 7.7 are allowed there.
3. Deye's product page for the SG04LP3-EU returns 404; Deye has replaced it with the SG05LP3-EU-SM2. Deye's DY-LV48-0128 list and the Dyness and Pylontech lists still name the SG04LP3-EU.
4. HVM 11.0 and Reserva 6.3 cap battery power at about 4.5 kW on the Fronius inverters. A 10 kW Symo kit gets full battery power only with HVS 10.2 (9.01 kW).
5. GoodWe + HVM 11.0 gives only about 5.1 kW of battery power (my estimate: 25 A x 204.8 V). GoodWe + HVS 10.2 gives about 10 kW (25 A x 409.6 V).
6. The 7-S1 has a single battery module, so with the Huawei M1 it is on-grid only. Backup kits need the 14-S1 or larger.

WHAT I CHECKED MYSELF:
- The researcher findings arrived truncated after the GoodWe block. There were no Growatt, BYD, Dyness or Pylontech researcher entries.
- Growatt: I took Growatt's side from en.growatt.com. The 2024-05 user manual and the datasheet MOD_3000~10000TL3-XH+ARK_XH_Battery.pdf (labelled 202307 on the product page) both give ARK-XH only and 600-950 V. The page also lists a 202608 BP datasheet, which I did not download; the BP figures in the voltage list come from the BP spec tables in that 2024-05 manual. The older 2022 manual (GR-UM-246-A-02) agrees.
- BYD V2.22 (2026-10-10): no Growatt or Huawei rows; Deye appears only with its high-voltage SG01HP3 models.
- Dyness LV list (15/07/2026): the only Growatt row is SPF 6K ES Plus.
- Pylontech LV list Ver.2.46 (2026-07-07): the Growatt rows are SPH, SPF and M-series only; the US5000 is listed for the Deye SUN-SG04LP3 series.
- Dyness G3 x Deye: I confirmed the tick in the 'Powerbox G3' column for SUN-5/6/8/10/12K-SG04LP3-EU on a rendered image of the Dyness PDF.
- Fronius: I re-checked the BYD solution sheet V13 (May 2026) and the Reserva sheet V10 (Dec 2025) rows against the table text.

NO SIDE CONFLICTS: wherever both makers' researchers covered a pair, their verdicts agreed. The only verdicts I changed are the two Fronius x LUNA downgrades described above.

DATES: no list I relied on is older than 2023. The newest:

sides.notes:
FRONIUS SCOPE: SUMMARY
Compatible:
- Primo GEN24 5.0 Plus + BYD Premium HVM 11.0 (4.51 kW)
- Primo GEN24 5.0 Plus + Fronius Reserva 6.3 (4.51 kW)
- Symo GEN24 10.0 Plus + BYD Premium HVS 10.2 (9.01 kW)
- Symo GEN24 10.0 Plus + BYD Premium HVM 11.0 (4.51 kW)
- Symo GEN24 10.0 Plus + Fronius Reserva 6.3 (4.51 kW)

Not compatible:
- Primo GEN24 5.0 Plus + HVS 10.2: Fronius explicitly excludes it. Only HVS 5.1 and 7.7 are allowed on the Primo; BYD allows 2-3 HVS modules on it, and the 10.2 has 4.
- Both Fronius inverters + Dyness PowerBox G3, Huawei LUNA2000-7-S1, Pylontech US5000: these are not on Fronius's closed battery list. Dyness and Pylontech are low-voltage batteries; Huawei's battery works only with Huawei inverters.
- Reserva 6.3 + Deye / GoodWe / Growatt / Huawei: Fronius lists only Fronius hybrid inverters for Reserva.
  - Deye: hard mismatch, its battery input is 40-60 V.
  - Huawei: hard mismatch, closed LUNA2000-only list and 600-980 V input.
  - GoodWe and Growatt: no explicit 'not compatible' sentence exists. The verdict rests on neither maker listing the pairing (GoodWe's list is a closed warranty list). Treat them as never-pair; downgrade to 'unknown' if your policy needs an explicit exclusion.

SOURCES (all on the makers' own domains; none older than 2023)
- Fronius compatible-batteries page: https://www.fronius.com/en/solar-energy/solar-solutions/solar-energy-storage/compatible-batteries
  - The old installers-partners/.../battery-overview and compatible-batteries URLs now 301-redirect here.
  - No revision date is shown (© 2026).
  - Its grid rows match the solution sheets exactly. HVS 10.2 is blank for Primo GEN24 Plus and Plus SC, and ticked for Symo GEN24 Plus/SC. HVM 11.0 and Reserva 6.3 are ticked for all four GEN24 Plus columns. The Symo Hybrid column is empty for Reserva.
  - Footnotes: '*' latest software through Solar.web; '**' depends on country-specific certification and availability. Albania is not a Fronius market page, so confirm with a Fronius distributor.
- Fronius solution sheets: BYD EN V13 (May 2026), Reserva EN V10 (Dec 2025).
- BYD HVS&HVM Compatible Inverter List V2.22 (2026-10-10). The BCU2.0 and non-BCU2.0 copies are identical.
- Ignore the older BYD lists that search engines still return (V1.3 May 2020, V2.0 Dec 2020); they are superseded.

CONDITIONS THAT AFFECT KIT BUILDING
1. Both catalogue inverters are the non-SC variants. For these batteries the SC variants behave the same, except that Primo GEN24 Plus SC also accepts Reserva 12.6.
2. HVM 11.0 and Reserva 6.3 cap battery power at about 4.51 kW on both inverters. A 10 kW Symo kit with either gets only 4.51 kW of battery charge/discharge. HVS 10.2 gives 9.01 kW.
3. Minimum BYD firmware:
   - Symo: inverter 1.9.7-0, BMU 3.13, BMS 3.19; parallel needs inverter 1.10.5-0, BMU 3.14, BMS 3.20.
   - Primo: inverter 1.11.6-0, BMU 3.15, BMS 3.21.
4. Battery communication is Modbus RTU (RS485) over a shielded 4-pole CAT5+ cable.
5. The Fronius solution sheets list a Fronius Smart Meter as required: single-phase for Primo, three-phase for Symo.
6. Parallel limits:
   - BYD: up to 3 towers with the same module count, and HVS cannot be mixed with HVM.
   - Reserva: up to 4 towers with the same module count, and total output is capped at 32 A.

SOURCE QUIRKS
- Both Fronius help-center pages print an orphaned footnote 5. On the Primo page it reads 'does not apply to … HVS 10.2, HVS 12.8, HVM 8.3, HVM 22.1 & LG RESU FLEX 17.2'. It is consistent with the tables.
- The Symo 10.0 Plus battery range (160-700 V) comes from the current Fronius help center. Some search snippets quote older 150-455 V figures, but those belong to the Primo.

Bottom line for the Deye SUN-10K-SG04LP3-EU (a 48 V low-voltage hybrid):

sides.notes:
Primary source: BYD Battery-Box Premium HVS&HVM Compatible Inverter List V2.22, updated 2026-10-10, from bydbatterybox.com/downloads. BYD publishes it twice, once for BCU2.0 and once as the legacy HVS&HVM list. I fetched both files and they have the same SHA-256 (3219ea66…a5d1), so the verdicts hold for both BCU generations. Older lists (V2.10 from 2023-01-30, V1.3 from 2020) are superseded; do not use them.

How to read the list:
- The HVS/HVM columns give the allowed module count per tower. HVS 10.2 = 4 HVS modules; HVM 11.0 = 4 HVM modules.
- Then come the minimum inverter firmware and the minimum BYD BMU/BMS firmware, for a single tower and for parallel towers.
- General rules: max 3 towers in parallel, every tower with the same module count, HVS never mixed with HVM. BYD also says to always install the latest Battery-Box firmware.

Result: 5 compatible, 7 not compatible.
- Compatible: Symo GEN24 Plus with HVS 10.2 and with HVM 11.0; Primo GEN24 Plus with HVM 11.0 only; GoodWe ET 5-10kW with HVS 10.2 and with HVM 11.0.
- Primo GEN24 Plus with HVS 10.2 is NOT compatible. HVS is limited to 2-3 modules there, and HVS 10.2 has 4. Fronius's own help-center matrix agrees (https://www.fronius.com/en/help-center/solar-energy/products/solar-energy-storage/solutions/byd/byd-battery-box-premium-hvshvm, no revision date, (c) 2026).
- HVM 11.0 sits exactly at the 4-module minimum for Fronius GEN24 and GoodWe ET. The kit must never ship with fewer HVM modules.
- GoodWe ET PLUS+: BYD's row says only 'ET (5-10kW)/BT'. GoodWe's own Battery Compatibility Overview V029.1 (2026-10-22) explicitly includes ET PLUS+ and ET PLUS+ (16A) in that column and marks HVS 10.2 and HVM 11.0 (ARM 11+). That file is hosted on goodwe.com.au but is GoodWe's global EN overview.
- Deye SUN-10K-SG04LP3-EU, Growatt MOD 10KTL3-XH and Huawei SUN2000-10KTL-M1 are NOT on BYD's list. Each inverter maker's datasheet names only other batteries: Deye's is a 48 V/40-60 V low-voltage input; Growatt lists ARK XH (and APX HV on its product page); Huawei lists LUNA2000-S0/S1. These not_compatible verdicts rest on absence from both official lists plus the maker's own battery spec, not on voltage alone.
- If the shop ever stocks the Deye HV hybrid SUN-10K-SG01HP3-EU-AM2: BYD lists HVS 2-5 / HVM 4-8 with FW 2001-C016, BMU 3.19, BMS 3.26.

Out of scope, for the other subagents: GoodWe V029.1 also lists Pylontech US5000, but only in its low-voltage ES G2/SBP G2 columns, not ET. It lists Dyness POWER BOX G2, not G3.

pairs.conditions: Listed by Dyness, the battery maker. Row 7 (DEYE) names the model group 'SUN-5/6/8/10/12K-SG04LP3-EU', which covers the EU 10K. A separate row covers the '-SG04LP3-EU-AM2-P' variant, also ticked. The list states no firmware requirement and no region limit beyond the EU suffix. Install conditions come from the Powerbox G3 User Manual V4.0 (2026-09-18). (1) On the master battery, set DIP switch #3 to ON: Deye is in the manual's '#3 ON' group, and the factory setting 0000 is only for Solis, GoodWe, TBB, SAJ and SolaX. Slave batteries stay at 0000. (2) Use the supplied communication network cable from the battery's CAN IN port to the inverter's CAN/RS485 BMS port. The label on the cable names the inverter it suits; for other inverters Dyness asks you to contact them for the pin order. Use the supplied power cables. (3) Sizing: the manual's Table 3-7 gives 1–2 Powerbox G3 for a 10 kW inverter. One G3 allows 200 A max continuous but recommends 100 A (0.5C, 5.12 kW). The Deye 10K can charge/discharge up to 210 A, so 2 units are needed to reach full battery power. (4) Paralleling: up to 50 units. With an inverter of 10 kW or less, the parallel cables are ordered separately. Above 12 units, fit a CAN terminating resistor on the last battery. (5) Voltage windows overlap: battery 44.8–57.6 V, Deye 40–60 V. Phase does not matter for a DC battery; the inverter is the three-phase LV model.

Neither is inferred from a voltage match.

Source used: the current Dyness low-voltage list, 'Last updated: 15/07/2026', uploaded 2026-07-27 to dyness.com/inverter-matching-list. It has a 'Powerbox G3' column, the 6th of 13 battery columns. Dyness's second matching-list page has no other low-voltage or G3-specific list, only STACK, PowerRack HV4, DL2.5 and a KOSTAL note.

How the list was read:
- The PDF is an Illustrator file with no text layer for the ticks. pdftotext gives only the model names, so the ticks must be read from a rendered image.
- I rendered the PDF locally with pdfjs-dist and @napi-rs/canvas, loaded read-only from another local project’s node_modules; no project files were changed. I zoomed into the Deye SG04LP3 row and confirmed the tick in the G3 column.
- Every cell I inspected was ticked: all 13 Dyness LV models against every listed inverter row. In practice the list is per inverter model, not per battery.
- The page has no footnotes on firmware, region or cables. The DIP and cable conditions come from the G3 user manual.

Things that could cause a false match in the catalogue:
- The G3 datasheet's 'Compatible Inverters: SMA/Victron/Ingeteam/Solis/GoodWe/Growatt/Solplanet/Luxpower/Deye/Apsystem etc.' is brand-level only. GoodWe and Growatt there mean their LV models (GoodWe ES/EM/SBP/EO/'GW ET LV 6-20kW'; Growatt SPH/SPE/SPF/SPM/WIT). They do not mean GW10K-ET (ET PLUS+) or MOD-XH.
- 'GW ET LV' and 'ET PLUS+' are different products. Do not string-match on 'ET'.

Gaps and caveats:
- For Growatt I could only read the 2022 AU datasheet, which is older than 2023. The 2023-07 and 2026-08 datasheets on en.growatt.com were not read.
- The Fronius, GoodWe and Huawei spec pages carry no revision date.
- I did not check the Deye side's own battery list; this verdict rests on Dyness's list plus the G3 manual.
- When I tried to open the Dyness list PDF in the Browser pane, the server answered with a file download and the pane showed the user a save dialog. If that dialog is still open, it can be cancelled; I did not retry.
